featured_reviews.name: Anil Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
My overall experience with the medical team and flight crew was positive. Both doctors were professional and caring throughout the transfer. Dr. Baig was particularly dynamic, attentive, and reassuring, helping to instill confidence during a stressful situation. Dr. Yadav was also supportive, competent, and compassionate. The pilot and co-pilot performed their duties excellently, and we felt safe throughout the journey.
The most important outcome was that the patient was transported safely and received continuous medical attention during the flight. For this, the doctors and flight crew deserve sincere appreciation.
However, regarding the aircraft itself, I would hesitate to describe it as a fully equipped ICU air ambulance. The cabin appeared somewhat cluttered and unorganized, making movement and working conditions less comfortable than expected. There was no visible inbuilt oxygen system, and certain ICU-related facilities seemed to be unavailable, requiring the medical team to manually manage and change equipment during the journey.
In general, a true ICU air ambulance is expected to function as a flying intensive care unit, equipped with features such as an inbuilt oxygen system with adequate backup supply, ventilator support, multi-parameter monitoring, infusion pumps, suction equipment, organized storage, sufficient working space around the patient, and dedicated power backup for medical devices. While the medical team handled the situation efficiently and professionally, the aircraft infrastructure appeared to fall short of these expectations.
I would also like to comment on the cost. Considering the facilities and infrastructure available on board, the charge of approximately ₹18 lakhs appeared relatively high. I fully appreciate that air ambulance operations involve substantial expenses, including aircraft operation, medical personnel, logistics, and emergency readiness. Nevertheless, the level of onboard equipment and infrastructure did not seem entirely commensurate with the amount charged.
My intention is not to criticize the doctors or flight crew, who were excellent in every respect, but rather to provide honest and constructive feedback regarding the aircraft infrastructure and overall value for money. It may be worthwhile for the management to review the equipment standards, cabin organization, and pricing structure so that the service can better meet the expectations associated with a fully equipped ICU air ambulance.
Overall, I remain grateful to Dr. Baig, Dr. Yadav, and the flight crew for their professionalism, dedication, and care. The patient was transported safely, which remains the most important outcome, though there is certainly scope for improvement in the aircraft's medical infrastructure and organization.

featured_reviews.name: Kimberley Parker
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely Pathetic!

I wouldn’t recommend this service to anyone. They came on the reference of a doctor at Holy Family Hospital; I lost a close family member last evening; had to call up Dr. Kumar and he promised to be with us in 15 mins or so. He failed to show up, sent his deputy instead, who am not even sure was a qualified doctor, he certainly didn’t seem like it along with a youth who looked decidedly shifty.
Im not one to judge people by their appearances but my instincts proved correct . The “Doctor “ did a cursory (few second) check and then started filling out paperwork, they charged an outrageous amount supposedly for the paperwork, report and entire after death process, including arranging an ambulance, cremation etc. The deputy doc took the money and told us hed arranged cremation at the Santacruz crematorium. He was out the door in a matter of 20 minutes or so and the youth had the temerity to ask for a tip, for doing absolutely nothing! Not a single receipt was provided either.

Imagine our shock then when after taking payment, an hour later Dr. Kumar calls up and informs us the Santacruz crematorium shuts at 7 pm, he said we needed to go to Shivaji Park instead. It was only us two sisters as our father was too old (and in shock) to accompany us. The ambulance arrived late, only 2 attendants showed up instead of the promised 3. They had not brought the correct material so took close to an hour to prepare the  material for our family members last rites!

Finally when we got into the ambulance they took it upon themselves to stop to fill Diesel. When we got to the crematorium.  The two attendants agreed to stay till after the cremation and even said since they were going back past our home they could drop us back, We thanked them and completed the last rites/ process.
Inside the crematorium, seeing that we were only two women alone , the demands for extra money from the inhouse attendants and harassment started. Which we refused to comply with.
When we stepped outside, the ambulance guys thought they would try their luck, and said “Madam give us something extra,for our hard work” so my sister gave them 500 each , even though Dr. Kumar had advised to only give them Rs. 500 between them. Then they said “Madam to drop you home it will cost Rs. 2000” At which point I snapped and told them to leave , we could order an uber at less than quarter the cost.
Please keep in mind this is nearing midnight at this point. The crematorium staff continued to ask us to tip the guys, and they said we had to bring several accoutrements like milk, incense etc, (We are Christian so this is NOT relevant)  I said I had no money left would return for the ashes the following day.
Which I did with a male friend , and this time, ashes were handed over without a peep about tipping or any accoutrements.

My point is this. Dr. Kumar clearly thought hed get away with this, the ambulance guys clearly thought theyd push their luck with two grieving women ditto the crematorium staff. While I completely understand that people earn a living and must be compensated, this kind of exploitation when people are at their most vulnerable HAS to be addressed and stopped. Shame on you!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Warning: Do Not Rely on This Ambulance Service in Critical Situations

I’m sharing this with the hope that no one else has to go through what I did.

My wife was in a critical condition, admitted to the ICU at Apex Hospital, Kandivali East. The hospital had a tie-up with ambulance care ambulance service, and unfortunately, both the hospital and the ambulance team proved to be shockingly unprofessional.

Initially, I requested a transfer to a nearby, better-equipped hospital. The ICU team agreed and called the ambulance. However, as my wife's condition worsened, I made the decision to shift her to Kokilaben Hospital in Andheri West—a far more advanced facility. What followed was deeply distressing.

- Misguidance & Fear-Mongering:
Both the ICU doctor and the ambulance doctor, Dr. Dhirendra Dwiwedi, tried to dissuade me from transferring her to Kokilaben, citing distance and time constraints. This was misleading—it was an intra-city transfer, not an inter-city one.

- Deliberate Delay:
After I insisted firmly on taking the risk, the ambulance doctor made me wait an additional 10 minutes just to write a handwritten disclaimer stating they wouldn’t be responsible for any mishaps. In a moment where every second mattered, this delay was inexcusable.

- Unprepared & Unprofessional:
Shockingly, the ambulance didn’t even have enough diesel. We had to stop at a petrol pump mid-transfer while my wife was on ventilator support. This level of negligence is beyond comprehension.

- Unjustified Charges:
The final bill was ₹7,500—despite the earlier agreed amount of ₹4,500 for a transfer to Kandivali West. The extra ₹3,000 for a slightly longer route within Mumbai was never explained transparently. When I raised this with the owner, he argued that the change in destination required refueling. That’s their excuse for wasting precious time during a life-threatening emergency.

This experience was not just disappointing—it was dangerous. In moments where professionalism, preparedness, and urgency are non-negotiable, this team failed on every front.

Please, do not trust this ambulance service in emergencies. Your loved one’s life may depend on it.
